topIssues.title: chore(op-node): Fix light-sequencer follow-source ↔ sequencer oscillation during recovery
topIssues.author: op-will
topIssues.body:
## Summary

When an op-node is both a sequencer and a follow-source follower (the "light sequencer" config), recovery from a divergence between its unsafe head and the upstream safe chain oscillates, making net progress of ~1 block per 2 poll cycles (~4s/block on a ~2s poll)
instead of converging directly. This roughly doubles convergence time and wastes a forkchoice reset on every other cycle.

Surfaced while de-flaking `TestSupernodeLightSequencerInteropInvalidMessageReplacement` (#21806). That PR fixed the test; this node behavior is unchanged and needs its own fix.

## Mechanism

FollowSource already forceResets onto the upstream on divergence (the #21119/#21155 fix), but the sequencer rebuilds a block on its own fork before the next poll lands — so the follower re-diverges and gets reset again. Net advance is ~1 block per 2 cycles:
convergence is bounded, not stalled, but runs at half the achievable rate.

## Proposed direction

Make the follow-source forceReset resist being clobbered by the next sequencer build during recovery — e.g. hold sequencing until the reorg consolidates (upstream safe matches locally), so the sequencer rebuilds from the settled head rather than racing the next poll.
Should roughly halve convergence time. Not a liveness bug — recovery completes — so this is wasted work, not a stall.

## References

- Test-side de-flake: #21806
- Prior follow-source reorg fixes: #21119, #21155

topIssues.title: Make op-deployer manage migrate build validator-complete OPCM V2 migration inputs
topIssues.author: wwared
topIssues.body:
`op-deployer manage migrate` currently constructs a single OPCM V2 `DisputeGameConfig` from `--dispute-game-type` and `--dispute-absolute-prestate`.

That shape is too narrow for the post-migration state validated by `OPContractsManagerMigrationValidator`. The validator expects the shared DGF to have both super-root game implementations registered:

- `SUPER_PERMISSIONED_CANNON` / type `5`
- `SUPER_CANNON_KONA` / type `9`

It also validates permissioned game args for type `5`, including proposer and challenger, but the current CLI arg scheme only supports bytes32-only fault game args. As a result, the CLI can report a successful migration while producing a state that fails the validator, for example `MIG-DGF-10` when type `5` is missing.

Problem areas:

- `op-deployer/pkg/deployer/manage/migrate.go` builds only one `DisputeGameConfig`.
- `op-deployer/pkg/deployer/manage/flags.go` models migration as a single `--dispute-game-type`.
- `op-deployer/pkg/deployer/integration_test/cli/migrate_test.go` checks only that a DGF address is deployed, not that the resulting state passes migration validation.

Suggested fix:

Update `manage migrate` so the CLI can build the full OPCM V2 migration input:

- Register both required shared DGF game configs:
  - type `5` with permissioned args: absolute prestate, proposer, challenger
  - type `9` with permissionless args: absolute prestate
- Choose `startingRespectedGameType` separately from the registered game set.
- Add/restore flags for permissioned game args:
  - `--proposer-address`
  - `--challenger-address`
  - likely separate cannon and cannon-kona prestate flags
- Remove or de-emphasize `--dispute-game-type`, since migration is not a single-game registration.
- Update integration tests to assert validator-clean post-state:
  - type `5` and type `9` registered
  - legacy types, including type `4`, absent
  - respected game type matches the requested mode

Acceptance criteria:

- `op-deployer manage migrate` can produce a post-migration shared DGF state that passes `OPContractsManagerMigrationValidator`.
- CLI tests cover both permissioned and permissionless starting respected game type choices.
- Integration tests verify the DGF shape, not just that a DGF address exists.

topIssues.title: [PCD] Re-order interop depset and prestate generation before deploy
topIssues.author: 0xOneTony
topIssues.body: Both the interop depset stage and the prestate generation stage already exist in the `op-deployer` pipeline today, but they run after `DeployOPChain`. In the new flow the prestate hash must be available before `OPCM.deploy()` is called, so both stages move ahead of the deploy. The depset stage continues to run unconditionally for every deployment, writing the depset to state.

topPRs.title: op-deployer: continue prepared chain deployments
topPRs.author: lumoswiz
topPRs.body:
**Description**

Adds `op-deployer continue` for prepared deployments. `prepare` now snapshots its canonical intent, predicted addresses, deployer, OPCM, anchor timing, and contract artifact digests. `continue` uses that snapshot as its authority and rejects drift before execution.

All pending chains are simulated and verified before any transaction. Each send rechecks the anchor and deployer nonce, checkpoints the chain only after a canonical receipt, and verifies live configuration from one L1 block.

Retries reconcile complete deployments, reject partial deployments, and redeploy a checkpointed chain only when its deployment disappeared while the prepared anchor remains valid.

**Tests**

Covers prepared-input and artifact drift, all-chain preflight, broadcast guards, exact configuration checks, retries, reconciliation, reorg recovery, the full workflow, and the CLI.

**Additional context**

Stacked on #21897. The starting anchor proposal and prestate remain in chain state because they are derived after address prediction. Other continuation inputs cannot silently diverge from the prediction, including across retries after chain state is normalized.

Across multiple chains, independent L1 transactions cannot be atomic. A later failure leaves completed chains checkpointed for retry.

**Metadata**

Closes #21669

topPRs.title: feat(op-deployer): commit prestates before chain deploy
topPRs.author: lumoswiz
topPRs.body:
**Description**

Moves interop depset generation before op-chain deploys. Adds `ChainState.Prestate`. Adds `op-deployer prestate`, which commits resolved prestates to chain state.

Prestate values come from the command flag or intent overrides. Conflicting values fail the command.

**Tests**

Adds coverage for depset ordering, prestate state persistence, source resolution, conflicts, and strict hash validation.

**Additional context**

This PR supersedes #21601 for #20911.

The prestate command should run after prepare and before deploy. If a chain has no prepared state entry, the command errors and names prepare. Chains with no prestate source are skipped. If no chains receive a prestate, the command fails.

Coming next: prepare integration. It will build and persist the depset during prepare. It will clear stale `ChainState.Prestate` when prepare re-runs. That work depends on #21560, which owns the prepare command and loop shape.

The deploy-time permissionless prestate check lands via #20912 / #21610. Permissioned chains never require a prestate. `ChainState.Prestate` also appears there.

**Metadata**

Part of #20911

topPRs.title: op-core: add OP tx JSON codecs and consensus receipt encoding
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
Part of #20264 (opgeth-decoupling: make op-service/sources the OP-aware eth client). First of three stacked PRs; the follow-ups make `op-service/sources` decode L2 blocks/receipts via these codecs and migrate op-batcher to payload-based block loading.

Adds to `op-core/types`:

- **`DepositTx`/`PostExecTx` JSON codecs** matching op-geth's RPC transaction wire format (validation arms mirrored field-by-field), incl. accepting-and-discarding the post-Regolith effective deposit nonce. `PostExecTx.Hash` hashes `0x7D ‖ RLP([Data])` — op-geth hashes typed txs over the inner struct's RLP, which for post-exec differs from the verbatim wire envelope.
- **`Receipts`**, a `DerivableList` for receipts-root recomputation with the three OP arms hand-rolled: post-Canyon deposit receipts (nonce+version in the hash preimage), pre-Canyon deposit receipts (nonce deliberately excluded — diverges from `MarshalBinary`, per op-geth), and `0x7D` post-exec receipts.
- **`Receipt.UnmarshalBinary`** for consensus-encoded receipts (`debug_getRawReceipts` path), routing `0x7E`/`0x7D` to this package.
- **`Receipts.Geth`**, a non-copying view of the embedded upstream receipts.

Everything is pinned byte-for-byte against op-geth by differential tests (removed at the final cutover); the deposit hash-preimage rules additionally get cutover-surviving tests.

🤖 *Co-created with Claude Fable 5*

topPRs.title: feat(op-supernode): HTTP-backed remote interop nodes
topPRs.author: opsuperchain
topPRs.body:
## What

Adds a **remote node** to `op-supernode`: a participant in the interop set that the supernode does **not** drive. Instead of running a consensus client for the chain, the supernode **polls a remote HTTP endpoint** for that chain's **finalized** initiating messages and seals them into the chain's `LogsDB`. The chains the supernode actually drives can then reference those messages as **executing messages**, exactly as they reference messages originating from driven chains.

The **wire protocol is the plugin boundary** — point a remote node at any server, in any language, that responds correctly:

```
GET {baseURL}/finalized?after={N}
200 application/json:
  { "blockTime": 2,
    "block": { "number": N+1, "hash": "0x..", "parentHash": "0x..",
               "timestamp": 1002, "messages": [ {"logIndex":0,"logHash":"0x.."} ] } }
  // "block": null  ⇒ nothing finalized after N yet
```

Only a real HTTP **client** ships in the binary — there is no mock in production.

## Design

- **`op-supernode/supernode/remote`** (production):
  - `Adapter` — the internal seam the ingester polls.
  - `FinalizedBlock` / `InitiatingMessage` — **normalized initiating messages** grouped into a finalized block; these are also the JSON wire types.
  - `HTTPAdapter` — the production adapter: configured with a URL, polls the protocol above, caches the reported `blockTime`.
- **`interop.remoteNode` + `Interop.AddRemoteNode`** (production) — the ingester: polls an `Adapter` and seals finalized blocks into the per-chain `LogsDB`, mirroring the driven-chain `processBlockLogs` path. **Finalized-only ⇒ no reorg/rewind handling.** Ingesters run as background goroutines started in `Start`.
- **`verifyExecutingMessage`** resolves the *initiating* chain's block time from either a driven chain or a registered remote node (the single behavioral edit to the validation path). Remote nodes only ever appear on the initiating/source side.
- **Config:** `--interop.remote-nodes <chainID>=<url>` (repeatable / comma-separated). The supernode builds an `HTTPAdapter` per entry and registers it.
- **`remote/remotetest`** (test-only) — a deterministic `http.Handler` implementing the protocol. Tests wrap it in `httptest.Server` and point a real `HTTPAdapter` at it, so the production HTTP path is exercised end-to-end. The Go linker keeps it out of release builds.

### Why the served messages are referenceable

`raftwallogdb.DB.Contains` recomputes the message checksum from the **stored log hash** + the DB's chain ID + the sealed block's timestamp. So whatever a remote node serves is referenceable by an executing message that carries the derived checksum — the supernode trusts the (finalized) remote node for its own chain's content.

## Tests

- `remote`: `HTTPAdapter` happy path against the test server (contiguous, linked blocks; `blockTime` cached; `block:null` ⇒ not-yet-finalized), plus non-200 and null-block handling.
- `interop`:
  - `TestRemoteNodeIngestAndContains` — server → `HTTPAdapter` → ingester → `LogsDB.Contains` round-trip (positive) + wrong-checksum rejection (negative), against a real `raftwallogdb`.
  - `TestAddRemoteNode` — registration, duplicate/driven-chain guards.
  - `TestVerifyExecutingMessageReferencesRemoteNode` — a driven chain references a remote node's message (served over HTTP) through the real `verifyExecutingMessage` path (positive + negative).
  - **`TestEngineVerifiesExecutingMessageFromRemoteNode` (engine-level e2e)** — a driven chain emits a **real `CrossL2Inbox` executing-message log** referencing a remote-node-served initiating message; the log is sealed through the production `processBlockLogs` path (real `DecodeExecutingMessageLog`) and validated by the real `verifyInteropMessages` engine. Asserts the block is **accepted** when the reference is valid (and that the block actually carries one decoded executing message, so acceptance isn't vacuous), and **flagged invalid** when the reference is tampered.

`go build ./op-supernode/...`, `go vet`, and `gofmt` are clean; adjacent `config`/`flags`/`supernode` package tests pass.

## Notes / follow-ups

- No real chains/binaries yet: the engine-level e2e drives the real verification engine (`processBlockLogs` → `verifyInteropMessages`) with mock chains. A full devstack e2e (real op-node/op-geth driven L2 + in-process supernode + `remotetest` server, with a real tx emitting the executing message) is a natural follow-up; the supernode already runs in-process in op-e2e / op-devstack.
- The protocol is intentionally minimal (single polling endpoint). Auth, batching (multiple blocks per response), and a metadata/handshake endpoint are natural extensions.

---
